# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s

  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 930
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/930
- **Title**: fix(925): never let a bash_job log IO failure reach the root zone
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/925-bash-job-crash` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +80
- **Deletions**: -10
- **Created**: 2026-09-24T19:02:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-24T20:19:45Z

## PR Description

Fixes #925

## Root cause

The background job log sink (`File.openWrite()` in `startShellJob`) owned no one:

1. **Open-class failures** — `_FileStreamConsumer` starts `file.open()` eagerly at `openWrite()` with no error owner attached until the first write. A failure (missing `.fah/bash_jobs` dir, permissions) surfaced as an **unlistened future** straight into fa's `handleUncaughtError` → `exit(1)`. Entire process dead.
2. **Write-class failures** (the ticket's ENOSPC, errno 28) — `writeFrom` errors escaped the sink the same way; `IOSink.write` is fire-and-forget and nothing listened to `done`.
3. **Settle corruption** — the unguarded `await _logSink.flush()/close()` ran inside the unawaited exit future: rethrew into the zone AND skipped `_settled.complete()`, leaving the job showing *running* on the job board forever. (Reproduced pre-fix: unhandled `FileSystemException` + 30s `settled` timeout.)

## Fix

# pr-930: fix(925): never let a bash_job log IO failure reach the root zone

## Description

Fixes #925

## Root cause

The background job log sink (`File.openWrite()` in `startShellJob`) owned no one:

1. **Open-class failures** — `_FileStreamConsumer` starts `file.open()` eagerly at `openWrite()` with no error owner attached until the first write. A failure (missing `.fah/bash_jobs` dir, permissions) surfaced as an **unlistened future** straight into fa's `handleUncaughtError` → `exit(1)`. Entire process dead.
2. **Write-class failures** (the ticket's ENOSPC, errno 28) — `writeFrom` errors escaped the sink the same way; `IOSink.write` is fire-and-forget and nothing listened to `done`.
3. **Settle corruption** — the unguarded `await _logSink.flush()/close()` ran inside the unawaited exit future: rethrew into the zone AND skipped `_settled.complete()`, leaving the job showing *running* on the job board forever. (Reproduced pre-fix: unhandled `FileSystemException` + 30s `settled` timeout.)

## Delivered

- Regression test `test/env/shell_job_io_test.dart`: an unwritable log path must yield a clean `Err` with **no unhandled error**. Verified failing-first against pre-fix code (unhandled `FileSystemException: Not a directory` — same class as the ticket's ENOSPC — plus the never-settling job), green after the fix. `BackgroundShell (local)` group 7/7, `shell_jobs_test.dart` 22/22, scoped `dart analyze` clean.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 930
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/930
- **Title**: fix(925): never let a bash_job log IO failure reach the root zone
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/925-bash-job-crash` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +80
- **Deletions**: -10
- **Created**: 2026-09-24T19:02:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-24T20:19:45Z

## PR Description

Fixes #925

## Root cause

The background job log sink (`File.openWrite()` in `startShellJob`) owned no one:

1. **Open-class failures** — `_FileStreamConsumer` starts `file.open()` eagerly at `openWrite()` with no error owner attached until the first write. A failure (missing `.fah/bash_jobs` dir, permissions) surfaced as an **unlistened future** straight into fa's `handleUncaughtError` → `exit(1)`. Entire process dead.
2. **Write-class failures** (the ticket's ENOSPC, errno 28) — `writeFrom` errors escaped the sink the same way; `IOSink.write` is fire-and-forget and nothing listened to `done`.
3. **Settle corruption** — the unguarded `await _logSink.flush()/close()` ran inside the unawaited exit future: rethrew into the zone AND skipped `_settled.complete()`, leaving the job showing *running* on the job board forever. (Reproduced pre-fix: unhandled `FileSystemException` + 30s `settled` timeout.)

## Fix

- `startShellJob` opens the log as a guarded `RandomAccessFile`: every open-class failure becomes a clean `Err(...)` (and the process is killed) instead of an async zone error.
- `_LocalShellJob` serializes log writes through a chain; every write error is consumed → `_logBroken` → the job keeps running headless, its log frozen at the last good chunk.
- The settle path drains the chain, swallows flush/close failures, and **always** completes `_settled`.
- Same-cluster: `SandboxShellJob.writeLog` (flutter_app) no longer poisons the write chain, and the WASI shell's `closeLog` guards flush/close so a broken log can't hang `completeWith`.

## Delivered

- Regression test `test/env/shell_job_io_test.dart`: an unwritable log path must yield a clean `Err` with **no unhandled error**. Verified failing-first against pre-fix code (unhandled `FileSystemException: Not a directory` — same class as the ticket's ENOSPC — plus the never-settling job), green after the fix. `BackgroundShell (local)` group 7/7, `shell_jobs_test.dart` 22/22, scoped `dart analyze` clean.

## Remaining / deferred

- No physical ENOSPC (errno 28) unit test: filling a filesystem isn't deterministically reproducible in the lane sandbox (hdiutil is blocked); the write path's never-throws property is enforced structurally (every write's error is listened) and the exception class is covered via the open-path regression.
- `jobs.maxLogBytes` size capping from the issue's proposal 2 is **not** included — it's a new config feature orthogonal to the crash; the process no longer dies either way. Happy to add if wanted.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless

Now I have the full picture of the WASI path semantics:

`_StreamSinkImpl.add(data)` → `_controller.add(data)` → lazily creates `_controllerInstance` and calls `_target.addStream(_controller.stream)` where `_target` is `_FileStreamConsumer`. 

In `_FileStreamConsumer.addStream(stream)`:
```dart
Completer<File?> completer = new Completer<File?>.sync();
_openFuture
    .then((openedFile) { ... })
    .catchError(completer.completeError);
return completer.future;
```

So when the open fails: `completer.completeError(e, s)` — a **sync** completer. `_StreamSinkImpl`'s `.then((_) {...}, onError: (error, stackTrace) {...})` — in the `else` branch (no new stream, not bound), `_completeDoneError(error, stackTrace)` → `_doneCompleter.completeError(...)`.

Now: `_doneCompleter.future` (i.e. `sink.done`) has NO listener at that point (nobody listens to `done` in `wasm_shell.dart`'s `startShellJob`; closeLog only listens later at flush/close time).

`Completer.completeError` on a future with no listener → when propagation runs (microtask), the error is reported to the zone as an **unhandled async error**. The listener-registration grace: Dart schedules propagation via `_Future._asyncCompleteError` → `_scheduleAsyncCallback`; if by the time it runs the future has a listener, it propagates to the listener instead. The listener here is registered only later when `closeLog` runs (`sink.flush()` → in `_StreamSinkImpl.flush()`, if `_controllerInstance != null`, it closes the controller → the addStream's controller-completer future completes → hmm wait.

Actually, careful: in `flush()`: `_isBound = true; var future = _controllerCompleter!.future; _controllerInstance!.close();` → returns `future.whenComplete(...)`. The `_controllerCompleter` was completed with ERROR earlier (from the addStream onError path when `_isBound` was false → wait no).

Let me re-trace the error path in `_StreamSinkImpl._controller` getter:

```dart
_target.addStream(_controller.stream).then(
  (_) {...},
  onError: (error, stackTrace) {
    if (_isBound) {
      _controllerCompleter!.completeError(error, stackTrace);   // forward to flush's future
      ...
    } else {
      _completeDoneError(error, stackTrace);   // completes _doneCompleter with error
    }
  },
);
```

When is `_isBound` true? `_isBound` is set true inside `addStream()` / `flush()` calls. In the job-log scenario: `sink.write(chunk)` → `add(data)` → `_controller.add(data)` (lazily wires `_target.addStream(_controller.stream)`) — note `add` does NOT set `_isBound` (only `addStream`/`flush` do; `_controller` getter throws if `_isBound`). So at the time the open-failure error propagates (microtask later), `_isBound == false` → `_completeDoneError` → `_doneCompleter.completeError(error, st)`.

`_doneCompleter` = plain `Completer()`. Its future `done` has no listener at that moment (nobody reads `sink.done` in the WASI job path). → **unhandled async error → zone handler → on mobile this kills/records the error** — same crash class the local path had!

Hmm wait — but there's a subtlety about when Dart reports "unhandled": for a `Completer.completeError` with no listeners attached yet, the error propagation is scheduled asynchronously; `_Future` marks the error as unhandled only if, when propagation executes, there are still no listeners. Actually the exact semantics: `_Future._asyncCompleteError` schedules `_propagateToListeners`; at propagation time, if `!hasListeners`, then `result._unawaited`? — no. Let me recall precisely: In `_Future._propagateToListeners`, when completing with an error and no listeners: `if (!hasListeners) { ... _zone.handleUncaughtError(...)` — it's scheduled via `_scheduleAgain`? The documented behavior: "If the future completes with an error and no one has listened by the next event-loop turn (when propagation runs as a microtask), the error is considered unhandled and passed to the zone's uncaught error handler."

Timing: the error propagation is a microtask. `closeLog` runs at job completion — potentially many milliseconds/seconds later (the whole job duration!). So if the log's initial open fails on the WASI path (bad path — but note: on WASI/mobile, `io.File` is available only where dart:io is; the wasm_shell uses `io.` prefix — mobile = real dart:io on iOS/Android), then the FIRST `sink.write(chunk)` schedules `_target.addStream(_controller.stream)`; the open fails; error completes `_doneCompleter` with no listener → **unhandled zone error, exactly the crash this PR exists to fix — still live on the WASI/mobile path.**

Hold on — is it really unhandled at that point? The `_then` registration: `_target.addStream(...).then((_) {...}, onError: ...)` — that's a listener on the addStream future. The addStream future is `completer.future` from `_FileStreamConsumer.addStream` — the error IS handled there (the `.then(onError:)` consumes it). Then the handler calls `_completeDoneError` which completes `_doneCompleter` — a DIFFERENT completer whose future has no listener yet.

`Completer.completeError` when the future has no listeners: the `_Future._asyncCompleteError` schedules propagation as a microtask; when it runs, if no listener was added in the meantime → `_zone.handleUncaughtError` → in the root zone → uncaught error → in Flutter debug it prints; in fa CLI, `handleUncaughtError` → exit(1). On Flutter mobile — unhandled async errors go to `FlutterError`/zone handler; per the PR description, fa's root-zone handler exits.

So YES: the WASI shell path still has the open-class unowned-failure bug — the very bug class this PR's local fix eliminates. The PR's own comment in wasm_shell claims the fix is about "a broken log sink must not break the settle path" (settle only). But the open-class failure on WASI: when does the open actually fail? `io.File(logPath).openWrite(mode: append)` — eagerly calls `file.open()` in the constructor → if logPath's parent dir doesn't exist → error completes `_openFuture`. At that moment, has `addStream` even been called? `_FileStreamConsumer._openFuture.then((openedFile) {...}).catchError(completer.completeError)` — wait, that `.catchError(completer.completeError)` is INSIDE `addStream()`, registered when the first write occurs. The constructor just stores `_openFuture = file.open(...)`. If the open fails BEFORE the first `addStream` call registers handlers... the open future gets handlers attached at first write. So:

- Open fails at time T0 (eagerly started).
- First write at T1 > T0: `addStream` attaches `.then/.catchError` to the already-failed `_openFuture` → since it's already completed with error, the `catchError(completer.completeError)` fires as a microtask → `completer.completeError` (sync completer) → the `.then(onError:)` in `_StreamSinkImpl` fires → `_completeDoneError` → `_doneCompleter.completeError` with no listener → **unhandled zone error** (unless `sink.done` was listened or flush happens in the same microtask window — it doesn't; flush happens only in closeLog at job end).

So on the WASI/mobile path, a bad log path → unhandled zone error → potential crash of the host app. This is a REAL gap in the fix the PR claims to cover ("Same-cluster: ... the WASI shell's closeLog guards flush/close so a broken log can't hang completeWith" — but the open-class error still escapes to the zone long before settle).

Hmm, wait — one more check: is it truly "no listener"? `IOSink.close()` (called in closeLog) returns `done` — but closeLog only runs at completeWith. Between the failing first write and job completion, `_doneCompleter` sits completed-with-error and unlistened. The propagation microtask runs immediately after → unhandled error. So the crash happens mid-job, NOT at settle. The `closeLog` guard is thus insufficient for the open-class failure on the WASI path. The severity: BLOCKING for the PR's stated goal ("never let a bash_job log IO failure reach the root zone") — the fix is incomplete for the WASI/mobile cluster. But the ticket/issue #925 is about the local fa process crash (ENOSPC); the WASI path is "same-cluster" hardening done by the author. running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 930
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/930
- **Title**: fix(925): never let a bash_job log IO failure reach the root zone
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/925-bash-job-crash` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +80
- **Deletions**: -10
- **Created**: 2026-09-24T19:02:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-24T20:19:45Z

## PR Description

Fixes #925

## Root cause

The background job log sink (`File.openWrite()` in `startShellJob`) owned no one:

1. **Open-class failures** — `_FileStreamConsumer` starts `file.open()` eagerly at `openWrite()` with no error owner attached until the first write. A failure (missing `.fah/bash_jobs` dir, permissions) surfaced as an **unlistened future** straight into fa's `handleUncaughtError` → `exit(1)`. Entire process dead.
2. **Write-class failures** (the ticket's ENOSPC, errno 28) — `writeFrom` errors escaped the sink the same way; `IOSink.write` is fire-and-forget and nothing listened to `done`.
3. **Settle corruption** — the unguarded `await _logSink.flush()/close()` ran inside the unawaited exit future: rethrew into the zone AND skipped `_settled.complete()`, leaving the job showing *running* on the job board forever. (Reproduced pre-fix: unhandled `FileSystemException` + 30s `settled` timeout.)

## Fix

- `startShellJob` opens the log as a guarded `RandomAccessFile`: every open-class failure becomes a clean `Err(...)` (and the process is killed) instead of an async zone error.
- `_LocalShellJob` serializes log writes through a chain; every write error is consumed → `_logBroken` → the job keeps running headless, its log frozen at the last good chunk.
- The settle path drains the chain, swallows flush/close failures, and **always** completes `_settled`.
- Same-cluster: `SandboxShellJob.writeLog` (flutter_app) no longer poisons the write chain, and the WASI shell's `closeLog` guards flush/close so a broken log can't hang `completeWith`.

## Delivered

- Regression test `test/env/shell_job_io_test.dart`: an unwritable log path must yield a clean `Err` with **no unhandled error**. Verified failing-first against pre-fix code (unhandled `FileSystemException: Not a directory` — same class as the ticket's ENOSPC — plus the never-settling job), green after the fix. `BackgroundShell (local)` group 7/7, `shell_jobs_test.dart` 22/22, scoped `dart analyze` clean.

## Remaining / deferred

- No physical ENOSPC (errno 28) unit test: filling a filesystem isn't deterministically reproducible in the lane sandbox (hdiutil is blocked); the write path's never-throws property is enforced structurally (every write's error is listened) and the exception class is covered via the open-path regression.
- `jobs.maxLogBytes` size capping from the issue's proposal 2 is **not** included — it's a new config feature orthogonal to the crash; the process no longer dies either way. Happy to add if wanted.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless

`HashlinePatcher`, stale tags reject before any write. Wired in

- `lib/src/tools/read_selector.dart` — `read` trailing selectors:
  `:N`/`:A-B`/`:A+C` (`..` alias), comma multi-ranges, `:raw`. A literal
  file named `x:1-2` wins over the selector. `offset`/`limit` must not be
  combined with a selector.
- `lib/src/tools/archive_reader.dart` — `read` inside archives
  (`a.zip:inner/entry`, `.tar`, `.tgz`), 256 MiB cap.
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/` — `read` SQLite targets (`db.sqlite`,
  `:table[:key][?params]`, `?q=SELECT`). FFI engine (`package:sqlite3`)
  exported only from `lib/io.dart`, passed via `builtinTools(env, sqlite:)`;
  without it a clean "not supported" note.
- `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart` — background shell jobs:
  `ShellJobRegistry` over the `BackgroundShell` capability
  (`execution_env.dart`; `LocalShell`/`LocalExecutionEnv` implement it,
  `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`/`SecretsExecutionEnv`/`MemoryExecutionEnv` and
  the app's `ProjectMountEnv`/`SandboxedExecutionEnv`/
  `PersistentWebExecutionEnv` forward it — the desktop app runs the host
  shell; mobile's `WasiSandboxShell` and web's `MemoryShell` run jobs as
  detached script Futures on job-local interpreter clones via
  `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/shell_job.dart` — own cwd/vars/capture, shared
  fs). `bash background: true` runs detached with output
  streaming into `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log`; `bash_job {status|output|stop}`
  (write tier) manages them. A settle fires `onSettled` on every exit —
  the CLI's terminal bookkeeping (`_onShellJobSettled`: job-board Running
  count, waiting row) hangs off it (issue #562). The model-facing notice
  (steered mid-run or a fresh idle turn; app `sendText` system-notice)
  is skipped when a foreground call consumed the result inline
  (`suppressSettleNotification`). Job logs on disk are NOT secret-redacted.
- `lib/src/tools/availability.dart` + `availability_gate.dart` —
  capability-gated tool availability (issue #19): `resolveToolAvailability`
  merges the `tools:` scope stack (global `~/.fah/config.yaml` < project
  `.fah/config.yaml` < session `.tools/<sessionId>.yaml` < runtime
  `--tools`/`FA_TOOLS`; deepest scope wins per key) over the host's hard
  capability floor — absent tools can never be force-enabled, unknown ids
  warn. The gate applies a resolution to the live registry idempotently

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 930
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/930
- **Title**: fix(925): never let a bash_job log IO failure reach the root zone
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/925-bash-job-crash` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +80
- **Deletions**: -10
- **Created**: 2026-09-24T19:02:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-24T20:19:45Z

## PR Description

Fixes #925

## Root cause

The background job log sink (`File.openWrite()` in `startShellJob`) owned no one:

1. **Open-class failures** — `_FileStreamConsumer` starts `file.open()` eagerly at `openWrite()` with no error owner attached until the first write. A failure (missing `.fah/bash_jobs` dir, permissions) surfaced as an **unlistened future** straight into fa's `handleUncaughtError` → `exit(1)`. Entire process dead.
2. **Write-class failures** (the ticket's ENOSPC, errno 28) — `writeFrom` errors escaped the sink the same way; `IOSink.write` is fire-and-forget and nothing listened to `done`.
3. **Settle corruption** — the unguarded `await _logSink.flush()/close()` ran inside the unawaited exit future: rethrew into the zone AND skipped `_settled.complete()`, leaving the job showing *running* on the job board forever. (Reproduced pre-fix: unhandled `FileSystemException` + 30s `settled` timeout.)

## Fix

- `startShellJob` opens the log as a guarded `RandomAccessFile`: every open-class failure becomes a clean `Err(...)` (and the process is killed) instead of an async zone error.
- `_LocalShellJob` serializes log writes through a chain; every write error is consumed → `_logBroken` → the job keeps running headless, its log frozen at the last good chunk.
- The settle path drains the chain, swallows flush/close failures, and **always** completes `_settled`.
- Same-cluster: `SandboxShellJob.writeLog` (flutter_app) no longer poisons the write chain, and the WASI shell's `closeLog` guards flush/close so a broken log can't hang `completeWith`.

## Delivered

- Regression test `test/env/shell_job_io_test.dart`: an unwritable log path must yield a clean `Err` with **no unhandled error**. Verified failing-first against pre-fix code (unhandled `FileSystemException: Not a directory` — same class as the ticket's ENOSPC — plus the never-settling job), green after the fix. `BackgroundShell (local)` group 7/7, `shell_jobs_test.dart` 22/22, scoped `dart analyze` clean.

## Remaining / deferred

- No physical ENOSPC (errno 28) unit test: filling a filesystem isn't deterministically reproducible in the lane sandbox (hdiutil is blocked); the write path's never-throws property is enforced structurally (every write's error is listened) and the exception class is covered via the open-path regression.
- `jobs.maxLogBytes` size capping from the issue's proposal 2 is **not** included — it's a new config feature orthogonal to the crash; the process no longer dies either way. Happy to add if wanted.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless

`HashlinePatcher`, stale tags reject before any write. Wired in

- `lib/src/tools/read_selector.dart` — `read` trailing selectors:
  `:N`/`:A-B`/`:A+C` (`..` alias), comma multi-ranges, `:raw`. A literal
  file named `x:1-2` wins over the selector. `offset`/`limit` must not be
  combined with a selector.
- `lib/src/tools/archive_reader.dart` — `read` inside archives
  (`a.zip:inner/entry`, `.tar`, `.tgz`), 256 MiB cap.
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/` — `read` SQLite targets (`db.sqlite`,
  `:table[:key][?params]`, `?q=SELECT`). FFI engine (`package:sqlite3`)
  exported only from `lib/io.dart`, passed via `builtinTools(env, sqlite:)`;
  without it a clean "not supported" note.
- `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart` — background shell jobs:
  `ShellJobRegistry` over the `BackgroundShell` capability
  (`execution_env.dart`; `LocalShell`/`LocalExecutionEnv` implement it,
  `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`/`SecretsExecutionEnv`/`MemoryExecutionEnv` and
  the app's `ProjectMountEnv`/`SandboxedExecutionEnv`/
  `PersistentWebExecutionEnv` forward it — the desktop app runs the host
  shell; mobile's `WasiSandboxShell` and web's `MemoryShell` run jobs as
  detached script Futures on job-local interpreter clones via
  `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/shell_job.dart` — own cwd/vars/capture, shared
  fs). `bash background: true` runs detached with output
  streaming into `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log`; `bash_job {status|output|stop}`
  (write tier) manages them. A settle fires `onSettled` on every exit —
  the CLI's terminal bookkeeping (`_onShellJobSettled`: job-board Running
  count, waiting row) hangs off it (issue #562). The model-facing notice
  (steered mid-run or a fresh idle turn; app `sendText` system-notice)
  is skipped when a foreground call consumed the result inline
  (`suppressSettleNotification`). Job logs on disk are NOT secret-redacted.
- `lib/src/tools/availability.dart` + `availability_gate.dart` —
  capability-gated tool availability (issue #19): `resolveToolAvailability`
  merges the `tools:` scope stack (global `~/.fah/config.yaml` < project
  `.fah/config.yaml` < session `.tools/<sessionId>.yaml` < runtime
  `--tools`/`FA_TOOLS`; deepest scope wins per key) over the host's hard
  capability floor — absent tools can never be force-enabled, unknown ids
  warn. The gate applies a resolution to the live registry idempotently

2. The `_LocalShellJob` settle path: `await _writeChain;` then flush/close in try. One more subtle thing: `try { await _logSink.flush(); await _logSink.close(); } on Object { _logBroken = true; }` — if flush succeeds and close succeeds, fine. If flush throws, close is never attempted → the RAF fd leaks (never closed). `close()` on a broken RAF returns Future.error(FileSystemException("File closed")) — harmless, but skipping close on flush failure leaves the fd open until GC/finalizer. Minor: put close in a separate guarded await or use whenComplete. Actually: `await _logSink.flush()` throws → jumps to catch → `_logSink.close()` never called → fd leak (one per broken-log job; process-lifetime). Since fa is a long-running process, repeated ENOSPC jobs could accumulate fds. It's minor but real — SUGGESTION (or IMPORTANT?). It's a resource-leak-on-error-path; low frequency; the process is likely also struggling with a full disk anyway. SUGGESTION.

3. `fanOut` — when `_logBroken` is true, skips writes but still appends to `_output` — intended (live output stream still flows).

4. Type regression check: field `final RandomAccessFile _logSink;` — `_logSink.flush()` exists on RAF (returns Future<RandomAccessFile>) — awaited fine.

5. Behavior change note: `IOSink.write` buffered/async fire-and-forget with internal buffering; RAF serialized chain adds per-write await overhead — one IPC dispatch per chunk vs the old sink's internal buffering (which also did per-chunk addStream→writeFrom dispatch; IOSink via _FileStreamConsumer does writeFrom per chunk too — same cost). No perf regression worth flagging.

6. `SandboxShellJob.writeLog` — `.catchError((Object _) {})` discards the error entirely (no `_logBroken` short-circuit and no surfacing). The local job at least freezes the log; sandbox jobs keep hammering the failing writer per chunk. For MemoryShell web, `_fs.appendFile` returns Result (never throws?) — the catchError is for the throwing WASI sink.write path. Consistency nit: could add a `_logBroken`-style flag for symmetry; not required. SUGGESTION-level at most. Actually — hmm, there's a subtle behavioral thing: for `SandboxShellJob`, `completeWith` writes `'[job error: $error]\n'` via writeLog — if the writer is broken, that error note silently vanishes. Minor.

Per rules: "Inline comments MUST target a line that appears in the PR diff. If the line is not in the diff, the comment becomes a general PR comment instead."

The `_logBroken`-related: local `fanOut` — one more check. `.then((_) => _logSink.writeString(chunk)).then((_) {}, onError: (Object _) { _logBroken = true; })` — the FIRST `.then` returns Future<void> whose error is handled by the second `.then`'s onError → chain never rejects → `await _writeChain` safe. 

But hmm — `writeString(chunk)` could throw SYNCHRONOUSLY? `writeString` → `encoding.encode(string)` — utf8.encode never throws (replaces unpaired surrogates). Then `writeFrom(data, 0, length)`: `RangeError.checkValidRange` — sync throw possible if end<start — impossible here. `_ensureFastAndSerializableByteData` — wrapped in try → Future.error. So no sync escape. Good.

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 930
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/930
- **Title**: fix(925): never let a bash_job log IO failure reach the root zone
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/925-bash-job-crash` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +80
- **Deletions**: -10
- **Created**: 2026-09-24T19:02:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-24T20:19:45Z

## PR Description

Fixes #925

## Root cause

The background job log sink (`File.openWrite()` in `startShellJob`) owned no one:

1. **Open-class failures** — `_FileStreamConsumer` starts `file.open()` eagerly at `openWrite()` with no error owner attached until the first write. A failure (missing `.fah/bash_jobs` dir, permissions) surfaced as an **unlistened future** straight into fa's `handleUncaughtError` → `exit(1)`. Entire process dead.
2. **Write-class failures** (the ticket's ENOSPC, errno 28) — `writeFrom` errors escaped the sink the same way; `IOSink.write` is fire-and-forget and nothing listened to `done`.
3. **Settle corruption** — the unguarded `await _logSink.flush()/close()` ran inside the unawaited exit future: rethrew into the zone AND skipped `_settled.complete()`, leaving the job showing *running* on the job board forever. (Reproduced pre-fix: unhandled `FileSystemException` + 30s `settled` timeout.)

## Fix

- `startShellJob` opens the log as a guarded `RandomAccessFile`: every open-class failure becomes a clean `Err(...)` (and the process is killed) instead of an async zone error.
- `_LocalShellJob` serializes log writes through a chain; every write error is consumed → `_logBroken` → the job keeps running headless, its log frozen at the last good chunk.
- The settle path drains the chain, swallows flush/close failures, and **always** completes `_settled`.
- Same-cluster: `SandboxShellJob.writeLog` (flutter_app) no longer poisons the write chain, and the WASI shell's `closeLog` guards flush/close so a broken log can't hang `completeWith`.

## Delivered

- Regression test `test/env/shell_job_io_test.dart`: an unwritable log path must yield a clean `Err` with **no unhandled error**. Verified failing-first against pre-fix code (unhandled `FileSystemException: Not a directory` — same class as the ticket's ENOSPC — plus the never-settling job), green after the fix. `BackgroundShell (local)` group 7/7, `shell_jobs_test.dart` 22/22, scoped `dart analyze` clean.

## Remaining / deferred

- No physical ENOSPC (errno 28) unit test: filling a filesystem isn't deterministically reproducible in the lane sandbox (hdiutil is blocked); the write path's never-throws property is enforced structurally (every write's error is listened) and the exception class is covered via the open-path regression.
- `jobs.maxLogBytes` size capping from the issue's proposal 2 is **not** included — it's a new config feature orthogonal to the crash; the process no longer dies either way. Happy to add if wanted.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 930
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/930
- **Title**: fix(925): never let a bash_job log IO failure reach the root zone
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/925-bash-job-crash` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +80
- **Deletions**: -10
- **Created**: 2026-09-24T19:02:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-24T20:19:45Z

## PR Description

Fixes #925

## Root cause

The background job log sink (`File.openWrite()` in `startShellJob`) owned no one:

1. **Open-class failures** — `_FileStreamConsumer` starts `file.open()` eagerly at `openWrite()` with no error owner attached until the first write. A failure (missing `.fah/bash_jobs` dir, permissions) surfaced as an **unlistened future** straight into fa's `handleUncaughtError` → `exit(1)`. Entire process dead.
2. **Write-class failures** (the ticket's ENOSPC, errno 28) — `writeFrom` errors escaped the sink the same way; `IOSink.write` is fire-and-forget and nothing listened to `done`.
3. **Settle corruption** — the unguarded `await _logSink.flush()/close()` ran inside the unawaited exit future: rethrew into the zone AND skipped `_settled.complete()`, leaving the job showing *running* on the job board forever. (Reproduced pre-fix: unhandled `FileSystemException` + 30s `settled` timeout.)

## Fix

- `startShellJob` opens the log as a guarded `RandomAccessFile`: every open-class failure becomes a clean `Err(...)` (and the process is killed) instead of an async zone error.
- `_LocalShellJob` serializes log writes through a chain; every write error is consumed → `_logBroken` → the job keeps running headless, its log frozen at the last good chunk.
- The settle path drains the chain, swallows flush/close failures, and **always** completes `_settled`.
- Same-cluster: `SandboxShellJob.writeLog` (flutter_app) no longer poisons the write chain, and the WASI shell's `closeLog` guards flush/close so a broken log can't hang `completeWith`.

## Delivered

- Regression test `test/env/shell_job_io_test.dart`: an unwritable log path must yield a clean `Err` with **no unhandled error**. Verified failing-first against pre-fix code (unhandled `FileSystemException: Not a directory` — same class as the ticket's ENOSPC — plus the never-settling job), green after the fix. `BackgroundShell (local)` group 7/7, `shell_jobs_test.dart` 22/22, scoped `dart analyze` clean.

## Remaining / deferred

- No physical ENOSPC (errno 28) unit test: filling a filesystem isn't deterministically reproducible in the lane sandbox (hdiutil is blocked); the write path's never-throws property is enforced structurally (every write's error is listened) and the exception class is covered via the open-path regression.
- `jobs.maxLogBytes` size capping from the issue's proposal 2 is **not** included — it's a new config feature orthogonal to the crash; the process no longer dies either way. Happy to add if wanted.
